**Q4: Open responses (verbatim)**

**Respondent 1:** Money is the main thing. If it costs more than bus fare I can't come, but I'd really want to help plan something, so I'd rather be asked to organize it than just show up.

**Respondent 2:** The same few people end up deciding everything, so I'd come to something that asks everyone to weigh in, even if it's less fun. Make it easy for newer members to join the planning.

**Respondent 3:** My work schedule is the biggest problem, and I can't always spend money on things. Free events on a weeknight would be the easiest for me to make.

**Respondent 4:** Game days feel closed off if you're new. If there's a beginners' bracket, I'd come and bring people who haven't played before.

**Respondent 5:** The club has gotten too casual. A paid, serious skills workshop would bring back members who want to get better at something, even if a few people drop off.

**Respondent 6:** I'd come if it's a real skill I can list on my résumé. Social stuff doesn't interest me, and I'm not spending money on anything without a clear payoff.

**Respondent 7:** Weekends are when I see my family, so a weeknight evening would work. Small groups are better for me than big events, and I don't like assuming everyone's free on Saturdays.

**Respondent 8:** Free events get treated as optional, so people don't show up. A small fee makes people commit, and I'd be more likely to come if I'd paid something.

steps.learned_between_rounds: Round 1 showed the workshop winning, but the open answers pointed to cost, newcomer inclusion and wanting a say. Round 2 therefore asked about fee mechanism, involvement and topic. Topics came back scattered, with a career-skills thread.
steps.limits: Only 8 people, so this is a direction and not a measurement. Most splits are 3-2-2-1. No single workshop topic won. The tool replies were labelled as practice Flashpoint stand-ins. I did not rehearse on personas. One email per person was left unused.
lessons: Ranking plus an open question worked: the open answers showed the real drivers (cost, inclusion, résumé value) that the closed options missed.
